tho: The sun peeks up where earth meets sky,
The morning mist goes drifting by;
Who rises early, fresh and keen,
Will reap a harvest full and green.
loiGiai: The sun has just lifted over the horizon, the night mist is melting away, and everything is waking up. This verse greets a fresh beginning: whatever yesterday was, it is over, and today is a blank page. Those who rise early and prepare well receive the whole of the morning light. Begin your work with a fresh heart and keep a steady pace; results will come like a full harvest after days of diligent effort.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: A breakfast with everyone at the table, a word of goodbye before work or school, is a simple way to keep the family warm.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: This is a good time to start something new or return to unfinished work. Pick the single most important task and do it first thing, while your mind is clear.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Sleep early to wake early, step outside for a little morning sun, stretch and breathe deeply. A regular daily rhythm is the foundation of lasting health.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Mornings are when memory is sharpest. Set aside a short time each morning to review, and studying will feel much lighter.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love also needs fresh beginnings. A sincere, simple message wishing someone a good day can be worth more than many fancy words.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money comes from steady effort every day. Make a clear spending plan at the start of the month and keep working honestly.

loiKhuyen: A new day is here. Rise a little earlier, do the most important thing first, and greet your loved ones with a smile.

tho: A dewdrop rests on tender green,
Still bright before the sun is seen;
Our bodies, too, are dewdrop-frail;
Sleep deep, eat clean, and health won't fail.
loiGiai: A drop of dew rests on the grass, clear and sparkling, yet fragile before sun and wind. The human body is the same: precious and in need of gentle care. This verse reminds you not to take your health lightly while busy with work. Care for your body as you would a dewdrop: eat wholesome food, sleep enough, move gently and keep a cheerful heart. When the body is at peace, everything else has firm ground to stand on.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Pay attention to the health of your loved ones, especially grandparents and parents. A reminder to drink water or a trip to a regular check-up is love in practice.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't skip meals or stay up too late because of urgent work. Keep regular hours and take short breaks; you will last longer and work better.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: This verse speaks mostly of health. Sleep enough, eat more fruit and vegetables, drink enough water. If tiredness lingers, see a doctor for peace of mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Studying late night after night wears the mind out. A good night's sleep helps you remember more than any all-nighter.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: A love as clear as dew should be guarded with gentleness. Don't let hasty words hurt each other.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Health is your most precious capital. Set aside a small amount for looking after it, rather than spending on things that quickly pass.

loiKhuyen: Go to bed thirty minutes earlier than usual tonight, and drink a glass of warm water tomorrow morning before the day begins.

tho: White clouds drift by on skies of blue;
They carry nothing, drifting through.
If worries crowd your heart today,
Let go like clouds and float away.
loiGiai: White clouds pass across the sky carrying nothing and clinging to nothing, which is why they can travel so far. This verse is for someone holding many worries. Some things cannot be changed right away, and dwelling on them only tires the body and weighs down the mind. Learn from the clouds: do your part fully, then gently let go of the rest. A lighter heart brings a clearer mind, and your health will improve along with it.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If something at home isn't to your liking, don't keep it inside forever. Say it gently or set it aside for a while, and everyone will breathe easier.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't carry every task alone. Share some with colleagues, focus on what you do best, and leave the rest for later.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Long worry affects sleep and digestion. Sit quietly for a few minutes each day and breathe slowly and deeply. If anxiety persists, don't hesitate to see a professional.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't worry ahead about exam results. Put your care into today's lessons; with a light heart, you will learn faster.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love should not be a burden. Let things flow naturally like drifting clouds, stay sincere, and ask for a little less.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't let money occupy your whole mind. Spend moderately with a plan, and handle the rest calmly.

loiKhuyen: Write your worries on a sheet of paper, circle what you can act on now, then fold the rest away and set it aside.

tieuDe: The South Breeze of Early Summer
tho: The summer breeze blows soft and cool;
Young leaves stir by the garden pool.
Love, like the breeze beyond the pane,
Will come in time; no wait's in vain.
loiGiai: The early summer breeze brings a gentle coolness and softly stirs the young leaves. No one can hold the wind, yet everyone feels it when it comes. This verse speaks of love and connection: it cannot be forced or hurried. Live well, keep an open heart and stay sincere; when the time is right, a good bond will find its way to you like a breeze crossing the yard. Waiting with trust and kindness is never wasted.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: A home needs cool breezes too: a light joke, an outing together. Don't let family life become only a list of duties.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Opportunities sometimes arrive as quietly as the wind. Keep your skills ready so you can take hold of them when they come.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: As the hot season arrives, keep your home airy, drink enough water and avoid the harsh midday sun.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't lose heart if progress isn't visible yet. Knowledge soaks in like a cool breeze; one day you will find you understand clearly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: This verse speaks mostly of love. If you are waiting, live joyfully and keep your heart open. If you are already with someone, stay gentle and keep score less.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money doesn't come from chasing the wind. Stay steady in honest work and turn away from offers to get rich quickly.

loiKhuyen: Don't force what isn't yet ready. Take care of yourself, live kindly, and keep your heart open like a yard welcoming the breeze.

tho: The spring rain whispers, soft and slow,
And soaks the earth so sprouts can grow;
So give each lesson all your mind;
Keep steady work, and blooms you'll find.
loiGiai: Spring rain is very fine and never pours, yet day and night it sinks deep into the soil and helps young shoots grow. This verse advises you not to dismiss small efforts. Every page you read and every task you do carefully today soaks into you like spring rain into earth. You need not achieve something grand in a single day; stay regular and patient, and the results will come steadily through the months and years.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Family bonds grow from small things: asking after each other daily, helping with little chores. Don't wait for big occasions to show love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Break a big job into small parts and finish one part each day. Consistency will earn you trust and clear progress.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Fifteen minutes of light exercise every day is better than one hard session and then giving up. Choose something within your strength and keep it regular.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: This is a good verse for study. Read a few pages and note a few ideas each day; keep at it, and your knowledge will fill up before you know it.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Lasting love comes from regular care, not big promises. Be gentle and be present when the other person needs you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Put aside a small sum each week, and in time it becomes a meaningful amount. Avoid borrowing to spend beyond your means.

loiKhuyen: Choose one small thing you can do every day, such as reading five pages, and keep it up for a whole month.

tho: The rain moves on, a rainbow glows,
In seven hues the bright arc shows;
A quarrel is a passing shower,
Then sunlight warms the clearing hour.
loiGiai: The rain has just stopped, the sun breaks through and a rainbow appears brightly across the sky. Without rain, there would be no rainbow. This verse says that anger and misunderstandings between loved ones are like a shower: they will pass. What matters is whether, after the rain, you are willing to step outside and see the rainbow. Be the first to offer peace, and everything will become clear and bright again.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If something hurtful has just happened at home, let everyone calm down, then sit and talk. A sincere apology opens the door to many good things.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: The recent difficulty has taught you something valuable. Write down what you learned so you can do better next time.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: After a tiring period, the body needs time to recover. Rest well, eat regularly and see a doctor if you still don't feel right.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: One disappointing exam doesn't define you. Look at your weak points, keep studying, and you will see progress.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If the two of you have had a small falling-out, don't let it linger. Gently share what you think and listen to the other person.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: After a tight period, things will gradually improve if you spend carefully and work steadily. Avoid spending to make yourself feel better.

loiKhuyen: Today, send a message or call someone you have been upset with; a simple question about how they are is enough.

tho: Across the porch the sunlight streams;
Mom airs the quilts, Gran sits and dreams.
Like sunlight, family love stays true;
Give back the warmth it gives to you.
loiGiai: Early sunlight spreads gold across the porch; Mom brings out the quilts to air while the grandparents sit and chat. It is a simple scene, yet full of warmth. This verse speaks of family happiness born from small, familiar things. Family love is like the morning sun: it never runs dry if we know how to receive it and give it back. Spend time with your family doing simple things together, and you will feel your heart grow warm again.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: This verse speaks mostly of family. Do something together with your family, like cleaning or cooking. What grandparents and parents need most is to have their children near.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Colleagues are like a second family. A word of thanks or a small helping hand makes the workplace warmer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A few minutes of early sun, a clean and airy home, and dry bedding are simple ways to keep the whole family healthy.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Ask your grandparents and parents about their life experience. Many precious lessons aren't in books but right at home.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love lasts when two people care about each other's families. Make time to visit the people your loved one holds dear.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: When the whole family plans spending together, waste is avoided. Simple joys rarely cost much.

loiKhuyen: This weekend, give one whole afternoon to your family: put your phone away and do a small task together.

tho: The full moon shines on high and wide,
It lights each road on every side;
Though loved ones live a world away,
We share one moon, and meet one day.
loiGiai: The full moon is round and bright, shining everywhere, not on any single roof. Even when loved ones are far away, everyone still gazes at the same moon. This verse carries the meaning of reunion and closeness. Distance doesn't fade affection if hearts still turn toward each other. Stay in touch and ask after each other often; the day you gather again will be all the fuller for the bonds you nurture today.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: For family far away, call regularly. For family nearby, share a full meal together on the night of the full moon.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Working with people far away needs clear communication. Keep in regular contact and share information openly so things run smoothly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: A beautiful moonlit night is a chance to relax with a gentle walk. Avoid staying up too late so your sleep stays regular.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Studying with friends, even online, helps you understand more deeply. Share what you know and learn from others.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If your loved one is far away, trust each other and keep your promises. Sincerity and regular check-ins help love bridge the distance.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Money matters between family should be transparent. If you need to help each other, speak clearly so the bond lasts.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, call a family member who lives far away and tell them one happy thing from your day.

tho: Before the dawn, the morning star
Shines small and faithful from afar;
So keep your study day by day,
And you will shine and find your way.
loiGiai: While the sky is still dark, the morning star already sparkles in the east, like a call for the diligent to rise. This verse encourages study and self-discipline. The star is small but faithful, appearing night after night; a learner needs that same steadiness more than short bursts of effort. Don't grow idle and don't lose heart; work a little every morning and evening, and your understanding will grow brighter.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Parents can set an example by reading and learning. When children see adults working hard, they naturally follow.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Make time to learn new skills for your work. Quiet preparation today will make you steady tomorrow.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Rising early is good, but go to bed early to get enough sleep. Don't trade sleep for overwork or overstudy.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: This verse speaks mostly of study. Make a fixed timetable, study every day, and review old lessons before starting new ones.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: A person with purpose who keeps improving is always attractive. Take care of yourself and value someone who shares your aims.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Learning a trade or a new skill is the surest investment. Don't believe promises of quick money without effort.

loiKhuyen: Set a fixed study time each day, even just twenty minutes, and keep it like an appointment with yourself.

tho: The spring returns and warms the land,
So till the fields with willing hand;
Good harvests don't fall from air;
So work and save, with some to spare.
loiGiai: Spring returns, the earth grows warm, and people go out to till and plant. This verse marks a good start for your livelihood, yet reminds you that a good harvest doesn't drop from the sky. You must plant diligently from the start of the season and know how to save and be thrifty, so that by year's end you have something set aside. This is a good time to make a clear plan for the whole year and follow it patiently.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Plan the new year together as a family and share the tasks clearly. When everyone contributes, the home will be warm and well provided.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A favorable time to begin a new plan. Set concrete goals, break them into months and check your progress often.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: The change of seasons can be tiring; keep warm, eat nourishing food and exercise gently so your body can adjust.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: The start of a season is a good time to choose a new subject or course. A firm start makes the whole journey smoother.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Spring brings fresh energy. Be open to meeting new people, but stay sincere and unhurried.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: This verse speaks mostly of finances. Work diligently, record your income and spending, save a portion regularly, and stay away from gambling and risky investments.

loiKhuyen: Write a spending and saving plan for the next three months, and begin with a small saving this very week.

tho: The noon sun blazes, hot and bright,
So drink and rest in shade's soft light;
The body needs a cool retreat;
Don't spend your strength in noonday heat.
loiGiai: At summer noon the sun beats down like fire, and travelers must find shade to rest and take a sip of water. This verse suggests you are working beyond your strength, like someone pushing on through the midday heat. Know when to stop, rest and look after your body. Human strength has limits; saving it today means you can still walk the long road ahead. Don't strain yourself just to finish things quickly.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Notice if a family member is working too hard. A cool drink or a reminder to rest is a very precious kind of care.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Having much to do doesn't mean doing it all at once. Set priorities and take short breaks to keep your strength.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: This verse speaks mostly of health. Drink enough water, avoid harsh sun and take a short midday rest. If dizziness or fatigue lasts, see a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Cramming overloads the mind. Split your study time and rest five minutes after each session to stay alert.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: When one of you is worn out, be patient and care for each other; don't let stress turn into quarrels.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't overwork for a little extra money at the cost of your health. Sensible saving lasts longer than chasing income.

loiKhuyen: Today, drink enough water, rest for a few minutes at midday, and cross one non-essential task off your list.

tho: The autumn sky is high and clear,
Soft breezes stir the branches near;
A quiet mind learns well and fast,
So clear your desk, and lessons last.
loiGiai: The autumn sky is high and crystal clear, a light breeze blows, and everything seems to settle. It is the finest setting for concentration. This verse speaks of study: to learn well, first the heart must be clear and the mind settled. Tidy your desk, put away distractions, then diligently take notes and read. When the mind is calm, knowledge enters quickly and stays long.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Families can give children a quiet corner for study. Lowering the noise and turning off the television during study time is a practical gift.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Your work needs deep focus. Set aside uninterrupted blocks of time for the difficult tasks.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Autumn air is dry; drink enough water, keep your throat warm and sleep on time to stay clear-headed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: This verse speaks mostly of study. Clear your study space, silence phone notifications, and copy the key ideas by hand to remember them longer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love needs clarity too. Speak honestly, listen with your whole heart, and don't let trivial things cloud your feelings.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Take time to sit quietly and review your income and spending clearly. A clear head helps you avoid hasty decisions.

loiKhuyen: Today, clear your study or work desk, silence your phone for one hour, and focus on a single task.

tho: The north wind blows, the cold sets in,
But homes prepared stay warm within;
In summer, gather wood and store;
Spend just enough, and fret no more.
loiGiai: When the north wind arrives, homes that prepared early stay warm together. This verse speaks of foresight with money. In good times, don't spend everything; set some aside, like someone storing firewood in summer for winter. Spend moderately and live simply, and even a meal of plain vegetables will warm the heart. Preparing today keeps you steady when hard times come.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: The family should talk together about saving and preparing for big things ahead. Agreement brings everyone peace of mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Prepare ahead for busy periods: learn more skills, organize your files and keep good relations with colleagues.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: In cold weather, keep your neck, chest and feet warm. Eat warm food, drink warm water and move gently indoors.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Review early; don't wait until just before the exam. Steady preparation helps you stay calm in the exam room.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Love needs care in ordinary times too; don't wait until problems arise to pay attention to each other.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: This verse speaks mostly of finances. Build a small emergency fund, spend with a plan, avoid borrowing and stay away from all forms of gambling.

loiKhuyen: Open a separate savings pot for times of need, and each time you are paid, put a small amount in before spending.

tho: The crescent moon, a slender brow,
Will grow full-round, though thin for now;
New love, like that young moon, is slight;
With patient care, it fills with light.
loiGiai: At the start of the month, the new moon is only a thin line like an eyebrow, yet it will be full and round by mid-month. This verse speaks of a newly budding love, still delicate. Don't demand completeness from the very start; patiently tend and nurture it each day with care and respect. Just as the moon fills night by night, love will grow if it is fed with sincerity.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: New family relationships, such as in-laws or distant relatives, need time. Be courteous and kind so you grow closer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: A new job brings many unfamiliar things. Learn from those who came before and be patient as things settle into place.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: If you are building a healthy habit, start gently and increase gradually; don't push yourself too soon.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Not understanding a new subject right away is normal. Learn a little each day and your knowledge will round out like the moon.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: This verse speaks mostly of love. Budding love needs patience. Listen, respect the other person's pace, and don't rush to make promises.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Your savings may be small at first; don't be discouraged. Keep adding regularly, and over time you will see them grow.

loiKhuyen: Don't rush what has only just begun. Do one small caring thing each day and let time do the rest.

tho: Dark clouds roll in at close of day,
Don't let your heart sink in dismay;
The wind will rise and clouds will part,
Untie each knot with patient heart.
loiGiai: This evening dark clouds have gathered and the sky looks gloomy. But clouds never stay forever; when the wind rises, they scatter. This verse is for someone facing obstacles at work. Don't rush into sadness or overthinking. Calmly look at the problem clearly, find its causes, then untangle it one strand at a time. Once you understand it fully, the hard task becomes clear and a way out appears.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If things are tense at home, don't jump to conclusions. Sit down, let each person speak fully, then look for a solution together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: This verse speaks mostly of work. Write down the problem, list possible solutions, ask someone experienced, then try them step by step.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Stress wears the body down. Go for a walk outside and breathe fresh air to clear your mind.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: If a problem won't come out, set it aside, do another, then come back. Asking teachers and friends is also a great way to get unstuck.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: A misunderstanding between two people is only a cloud. Ask clearly instead of guessing, and things will become plain.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: If money is tight, sit down and review your income and spending, cut what isn't needed, and avoid quick loans or games of chance.

loiKhuyen: Write the problem you are stuck on, break it into three small steps, and take the first step today.

tho: A sudden storm comes rolling in,
With thunder's crash and lightning's din;
If harsh words slip at home one day,
Be still, and love will find its way.
loiGiai: Summer storms often arrive without warning, with crashing thunder and flashing lightning, yet they pass in moments. This verse speaks of times when harsh words slip out at home. Anger is like a storm: it comes fast and leaves fast, if we wait quietly for it to pass instead of adding more words. Afterwards, gently make peace; family love runs deep, and a single step of yielding brings back the warmth of before.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: This verse speaks mostly of family. When angry, step away for a moment and breathe deeply. Once calm, apologize first and talk gently.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: If there is conflict at work, don't react at once. Wait a little to settle, then speak frankly and politely.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Frequent anger affects blood pressure and sleep. Practice slow breathing when you feel anger rising.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: When frustrated by a hard problem, take a break, drink some water, then return. A calm mind will find the way.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: After an argument, don't let anger last the night. A sincere apology or a gentle hug can melt any knot.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't make money decisions while angry or upset. Wait until your mind is calm before deciding.

loiKhuyen: When you feel about to lose your temper, count slowly to ten and breathe deeply before saying anything.

tieuDe: The First Chill of Autumn Wind
tho: The autumn wind brings early chill,
Gold leaves are drifting down the hill;
When missing someone, write and say
A caring word to warm their day.
loiGiai: The first cool autumn wind arrives, the air turns crisp and golden leaves fly. It is the time to add a layer of clothing, and also a time when we easily miss someone dear. This verse reminds you of two things: keep your body warm and keep your affections warm. A well-timed word of concern can be warmer than a thick coat. Don't hesitate to show you care, and don't forget your own health as the seasons change.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: As it turns cold, remind your family to dress warmly, especially the elderly and children. A pot of hot rice porridge is also a word of love.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Asking after a colleague who is tired or going through a hard time makes the workplace warmer and closer.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Seasonal changes bring colds. Keep your neck warm, sleep enough and eat well. If a cough or fever persists, see a doctor.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Cool weather makes focus easier. Study in the mornings, but remember to dress warmly and not stay up late.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If you miss someone, gently reach out. Sincere, timely care is how lasting affection is built.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Preparing what you need for the cold season early saves more than rushing to buy when the need arrives.

loiKhuyen: Today, send a word of greeting to the friend you have been missing, and remember an extra layer when you go out.

tho: The morning fog hides every lane,
So slow your steps, no need to strain;
When work's unclear and you're unsure,
Ask those who know, and step secure.
loiGiai: In the early morning, thick fog hides the view ahead. Yet a traveler need not see the whole road, only a few steps ahead, and to walk more slowly. This verse is for someone hesitating because their work is unclear. Don't stand still waiting for everything to become clear; ask people who know, take firm steps one by one, and observe as you go. The fog will lift as the sun rises.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If you are unsure how to handle a family matter, ask the elders, discuss it with everyone, and decide one thing at a time.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: This verse speaks mostly of work. When the direction is unclear, do the certain parts first, ask experienced people and write down what you learn.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Keep warm when going out on foggy mornings. If your body shows unusual signs you don't understand, see a doctor for advice.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: If you are unsure which field or path to choose, research, ask teachers and those ahead of you, and try small things first.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: If feelings are still unclear, don't rush to conclusions. Take time to understand each other better, step by step.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: When you don't fully understand an investment or a large expense, it is best not to proceed yet. Ask someone knowledgeable and weigh it carefully.

loiKhuyen: Don't wait to see the whole road. Choose one small, certain step, ask one person who knows the work, then begin.

tho: The rain has stopped, the sky is clear;
On every leaf, bright drops appear.
The body, healing, still is frail;
Rest some days more, till you are hale.
loiGiai: The rain has stopped, the sky is bright again and the air is fresh. This verse is for someone who has just come through a period of tiredness, illness or stress. Things are slowly getting better, but the body still needs time to recover. Don't rush back into work as before; rest a few more days, eat nourishing food and step outside to breathe fresh air. Slow, steady recovery is the kind that lasts.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: If a family member has just recovered, take on some of their chores, look after their meals and let them rest fully.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: After a stressful period, return to work gradually. Rearrange your schedule and reduce non-urgent tasks to save your strength.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: This verse speaks mostly of health. Rest enough, attend follow-up visits as your doctor advises, and don't stop medicine or take on heavy work too soon.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: If you fell behind while sick, don't worry. Ask friends and teachers, and catch up gradually rather than all at once.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: After days of quarrel or distance, give each other time. Gentleness helps love heal.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: After a hard period, rebalance your spending slowly. Don't rush into big purchases or try to make up losses with risky moves.

loiKhuyen: Allow yourself more rest. Tomorrow morning, step outside to breathe for five minutes and eat a nourishing breakfast.

tho: On a clear night the stars shine bright,
Each with its own and gentle light;
Each learner grows at their own pace;
Don't measure friends, shine in your place.
loiGiai: On a clear night the sky is full of stars. Each has its own brightness, none competes with another, and together they make the sky sparkle. This verse speaks of study and self-confidence. Everyone has their own strengths and pace of progress. Don't compare yourself with friends and then feel sad; find what you are good at, develop it diligently, and you will shine in your own way.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Parents, don't compare your child with other children. Praise their strengths and patiently help where they are still weak.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Each person on a team has their own strengths. Do your part well and respect what others contribute.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Don't force yourself into someone else's exercise routine. Choose what suits your strength and age.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: This verse speaks mostly of study. Compare yourself with who you were yesterday. Find a subject you love, go deep, and help friends when you can.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't compare your loved one with others. Everyone has precious qualities; treasure what that person brings you.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Don't follow other people's spending habits. Living within your means keeps your finances steady.

loiKhuyen: Tonight, write down three things you do better than last month. Compared with yourself, you have grown more than you think.

tho: The evening sun fades from the eaves;
Our parents age like autumn leaves.
Go home while daylight still is here;
Sit close, and hold their love so dear.
loiGiai: Evening sunlight fades on the western porch, like parents' hair growing grayer each day. The love parents hold for their children is always full, yet the time we have together is limited. This verse gently reminds you: go home to visit and sit beside your parents and grandparents while you still can. No grand gifts are needed; just be there, ask after them and listen. That is the most meaningful gift for the elderly.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: This verse speaks mostly of family. Make time to visit your parents and grandparents; if you live far away, call regularly and listen to their stories.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Work is important, but don't let it take all the time meant for family. Keep a balance between work and home.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Remind your parents to have regular check-ups and walk gently with them in the evenings. Keep yourself healthy too, so you can care for your family.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Ask your grandparents and parents about the old days. Their stories are life lessons that books rarely hold.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Someone who loves their parents usually knows how to love others. Visit both families together with your loved one.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Set aside a small part of your income to care for your parents in practical ways, such as medicine and everyday necessities.

loiKhuyen: This week, visit or call your parents or grandparents, and spend at least fifteen minutes simply listening.

tho: The steady rain falls soft and slow,
Yet fills the fields where waters flow;
So study soaks until you know,
And savings, bit by bit, will grow.
loiGiai: A long steady rain doesn't pour; it simply patters day after day, yet the fields fill with water and the soil drinks deep. This verse says that lasting results come from regularity. Study that soaks in slowly leads to deep understanding; money gathered bit by bit becomes real savings. Don't expect everything at once, and don't trust shortcuts to quick wealth. Be patient and diligent, and let time help you build up.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Good household habits, like eating together and cleaning together, become a warm family rhythm when kept regularly.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Don't be impatient for promotion. Do each small task well every day, and your reputation and experience will build up.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Good health doesn't come from a crash diet or intense training, but from healthy habits kept over the long term.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Study a little each day and review often. Knowledge that soaks in slowly lasts longer than cramming before exams.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Deep love is nourished by small acts of care every day, not by grand promises.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: This verse speaks mostly of finances. Save regularly, even if little. Stay away from gambling, risky investments or promises of unusually high returns.

loiKhuyen: Choose a fixed weekly saving amount and a fixed daily study habit, and keep both steady.

tho: The waning moon will fill again;
Love, out of step, will still remain.
Anger, like wind on water, goes;
Give way one step: the moonlight glows.
loiGiai: The moon wanes and waxes; that is the way of nature. Love is the same: at times full, at times lacking because of misunderstanding or distance. This verse advises you not to think everything is lost because of one waning phase. If your heart stays faithful, and you learn to wait, understand and give way to each other a little, love will grow full again like the moon at mid-month.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Family relationships sometimes grow cool. Be patient and show care first, and the gaps will slowly be filled.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Work has its ups and downs. A slower period is a good time to learn and prepare for the next stretch.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Health rises and falls with the seasons. Listen to your body, rest when tired and see a doctor when needed.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Results are sometimes disappointing. Don't give up; review how you study and, with persistence, results will improve.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: This verse speaks mostly of love. If there is distance between you, talk sincerely, listen, and each give way one step.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: Income varies from month to month. Save in the good months so you have enough in the lean ones, and spend with a plan.

loiKhuyen: Give way to your loved one on one small matter today, and tell them one thing you truly appreciate about them.

tho: At midnight shines the northern star;
It guides night travelers near and far.
Study's a journey: know your way,
And long roads shorten day by day.
loiGiai: In the middle of the night, the northern star shines clearly, helping night travelers find their direction without fear of getting lost. This verse speaks of the importance of goals. A person with a clear goal knows where they are going, whether the road is long or short. Decide what you truly want in study and work, write it down, and let it guide you whenever you hesitate. With direction, no effort is wasted.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Set a shared family goal, such as saving for a child's education or repairing the house, so everyone works toward it together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Set clear goals for this year, broken into monthly goals and weekly tasks. With direction, you will be less scattered.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: Specific health goals, such as walking daily or sleeping before eleven, are easier to keep than vague wishes.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Work out why you are studying and which field you want to follow. A clear goal gives you motivation and helps you choose what to learn.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Share your plans for the future with each other. Looking in the same direction makes love more lasting.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: A specific saving goal, such as a fund for study or emergencies, helps you resist unnecessary spending.

loiKhuyen: Write down one goal for this year and three small things to do this month to move closer to it.

tho: The wind will shift without a sign,
Now up, now down, none can divine;
With money, don't just chase the crowd;
Save steadily, though winds blow loud.
loiGiai: The wind blows one way, then turns another, hard to predict. Money matters are the same, sometimes favorable, sometimes not. This verse advises you not to chase passing winds, such as invitations to get rich quickly or games of chance. Keep a steady rhythm: work honestly, save bit by bit, and discuss large expenses with your family first. Standing firm like this, you need not fear when the wind changes.

loiGiaiTheoChuDe.gia-dao: Agree as a family on how to spend, and keep a shared emergency fund. When hard times come, working together will see you through.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.cong-viec: Work may change. Keep learning new skills to adapt, and don't depend on a single source.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.suc-khoe: When the weather changes unpredictably, keep warm, eat regularly and rest enough so your body can adapt.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.hoc-hanh: Don't chase every study trend. Choose a direction that suits you and pursue it with persistence.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tinh-duyen: Don't let outside gossip shake your relationship. Trust each other and speak openly together.
loiGiaiTheoChuDe.tai-loc: This verse speaks mostly of finances. Stay away from gambling, trend-chasing investments or borrowing to speculate. Save regularly and spend only after careful thought.

loiKhuyen: Before any large expense or investment, wait three days and ask the opinion of a family member you trust.
